chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Circus and show bands that required reading; George Baquet and Jim Williams
summary: A circus band meant you had to read; Foster admires George (Baquet) and the top men in a touring show band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit

blocks.x: Now when you, now when you go, now there was a, there was a circus band, now if you couldn't read, don't even go in that band. See, because you had to read.

P.G. Laurel. Yeah. See, now, all them guys, now George, George, back there, I was, George, back there was like a picture on the wall of me. I just thought he was the greatest thing in the world, George. And George was a nice man. Oh, yes. I met him too. And I don't care where you was playing, if you knew you was in that band from New Orleans, he, he, he, he'd come there to see you. George got up out of his sick bed when he first got a stroke, come down, I played a concert, walked in there, looked at me. Shake his head three, four times, they'd tell you hello.
In Philadelphia. Philadelphia, yeah. That's where I saw him. A couple of times, never got to talk to him very much.

George, and, and, and, and Jim Williams, and Baptiste, there was three real top-notch men in a Joan and Roe show band. Now, that, there was a band, you, you get the music, see, Joan and Roe, she'd pass out the music, yeah. Get new numbers, pass, yeah. Joan and Roe, she'd start with that band. George Cross and Lake, look at that music, Mary, what? Played like, it's like you played blues or anything else.
